title: What to watch at the open
text: Yesterday's close: the S&P 500 fund SPY ended at $772.31 and the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ at $725.61. Two big tech companies, Alphabet and Microsoft, reported results after the market closed. Microsoft's stock rose in after hours trading, so watch whether Microsoft and the AI group follow through at the open. Early moves can reverse by the afternoon. This is for learning, not advice.

title: Microsoft's cloud grows faster
text: Microsoft said its cloud business Azure grew 48% from a year ago, faster than the 42% of the last quarter. Total sales were about $92.3 billion, up 19%. The stock closed at $531.01 on Wednesday, before the news, and reports say it rose about 4% after the close. Azure is the 'rented computers' business that companies use to build AI.

title: Alphabet reports big sales growth
text: Alphabet, the parent of Google, said its sales grew 25% to about $127.6 billion. Its stock closed at $324.89, up 1.3%, before the report came out. Alphabet is 20% below its 52 week high of $408.61. The 52 week range is the lowest and highest price in the past year, so it shows how far a stock has pulled back.

title: Vertiv's jump: will it last?
text: Vertiv closed at $242.94 on Wednesday, up 16.5%, after it raised its forecast. It makes power and cooling gear for data centers. A jump that big often calms down in the days after, and the stock is still 36% below its 52 week high. Its beta of 2.05 means it moves about twice as much as the market.

title: Lesson 28: What is guidance?
text: Guidance is a company's own forecast of its sales or profit for the next few months. Think of a student who says, 'I expect to get a B on the next test.' If the student gets an A, people are happy. If it is a C, people are let down. Investors pay close attention to guidance because stocks are about the future. Microsoft's forecast this week said it expects its sales to grow 18% to 19% next quarter. A company can have a great past quarter and still see its stock fall if its guidance sounds weak. Remember that a forecast is a guess, not a promise.
